geometry_edits.rationale: Translate the dominant book cut into a corner cut so the mass reads as one cohesive block with a clearer entry void instead of a generic slice.
Use the access-adjacent corner to strengthen the public threshold.
Make the corner cut large enough to read in all four views while keeping the primary mass dominant.
Bound the cut so it stays structural and does not fragment the mass.
Tighten the courtyard to improve enclosure and public legibility.
Keep the opening aligned to the access side so the ground response remains explicit.

rationale: The candidate reads as a compact, coherent neighborhood mass with a clear dominant block, and the courtyard/void logic is visible in all four views rather than only one. The blue frontage edge is answered by an open seam and setback at the ground, so the access response is semantically aligned rather than sealed. It is somewhat box-driven and the section is modest, but the massing still supports the program: active ground threshold, one clear void, and a calm upper volume. No obvious cross-view collisions are visible, and the parcel is contained. The form is not especially inventive, but it is legible and program-appropriate.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Reference is more sculptural/cultural than the candidate, but the public void and bridge logic are transferable.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Three-part massing with a legible central void and an upper connector can support an active neighborhood program.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Much larger and more campus-like than this compact candidate; do not copy the perimeter complexity.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Courtyard-centered campus-like arrangement with stepped low-rise pieces can organize public circulation.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: The candidate is more compact and boxy; avoid assuming transparency or long-span roof language.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Elongated low-rise massing with a courtyard void and horizontal spread fits mixed neighborhood use.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: This reference is more topographic and loose; the candidate should stay more anchored and less fragmented.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Terraced/ribbon-like massing with connected wings and a central open space offers a strong precedent for sectional hierarchy.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Reference complexity is higher; the candidate should not over-fragment into multiple disconnected wings.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Interlocking volumes with a courtyard and voids under elevated blocks can create a robust public threshold.

warnings: The silhouette is still somewhat generic and rectangular; it relies on void carving more than on a strongly profiled section.
The step/roof articulation is restrained enough that it could drift toward bland boxiness if not refined further.
